Why this assessment?

Students show what they have learned, practise speaking in front of an audience, and build confidence. Coaches use the results to see each child’s progress and next steps.

Rules & attire

  • Only invited existing Ebright students can join.
  • Students present a prepared speech based on their age group and the Chapter 11 topic of their grade.
  • Props are allowed. Reading from a script or flashcards is not allowed.
  • Ebright will not write the speech for participants.

Attire

  • Smart casual (red or Ebright shirt) or semi-formal. Accessories are welcome.
  • Boys: collared shirt with slacks. Girls: neat dress, or blouse with slacks.
  • No shorts or slippers.
  • Special costume? Inform the showcase PIC beforehand for approval.
  • Grade 5 (Emcee): formal or semi-formal. Blazer or traditional clothes.

Example of attire for showcase

Rewards

Foundation Appraisal Certificate + Medal + Microphone + FA Assessment Report (grading).

How your child is marked

Four areas, 25 marks each. Pass: 15–18 per area. Distinction: 19–25.

Communication · 25Clear, organised ideas; understands the topic; speaks confidently.
Analysis · 25Grasps the big idea; thinks critically; backs up points with reasons.
Interaction · 25Listens, responds, collaborates and adjusts.
Performance · 25Confidence, clear and engaging voice, gestures and expressions.

Preparing at home

  • Don’t memorise word for word. A natural, flowing speech scores better.
  • Draft a bullet-point outline, or draw small images as memory cues.
  • Structure: OCC and PREP (Point, Reason, Example, Point) are the basics. Chronological, spatial, problem–solution and cause–effect orders are also fine.
  • Need more practice? Ebright offers an extra online session, and parents can send practice videos for coach review.

Simple speech outline

OpeningGreeting, name, topic
ContentPREP #1, #2, #3: “Firstly… This is because… For example… That’s why…”
Conclusion“In conclusion, I… Thank you.”

Sample scripts are for structure only. Students should use their own ideas and sound natural.

Questions & contact

Can my child read from notes?

No scripts or flashcards. A bullet outline or drawn cues for practice are encouraged, but the speech is delivered without reading.

Do we need to bring props?

Grades 2, 3 and 4 require pictures or functional props. Check your grade’s card in the first tab.

Can my child wear a costume?

Yes. Grade 6 requires one. For other grades, ask the showcase PIC for approval first.

Can any student join Grades 9–12?

No. These advanced grades are by special invitation only, not the regular showcase.
